paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: the One on the throne is in charge, and He is worthy of all our worship. The elders cast their golden crowns before Him, and I can't even give up the last crumb of a cookie (Revelation 4:10). They tell us why: "You created all things; by Your will they exist and were created." (Revelation 4:11) Everything starts with Him, so everything bows to Him.

Then comes the scary part, when no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth can open the scroll, and John weeps bitterly (Revelation 5:3-4). Even with all that glory in the room, the problem is real. But the elder says, "Do not weep!" and John turns to see a Lamb who appeared to have been slain (Revelation 5:5-6). The Lamb is worthy because of what He did: "You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation." (Revelation 5:9)

Here's why that matters to you, friend. You don't have to be worthy enough yourself, because the Lamb already is, and His people come from every tribe and tongue and people and nation (Revelation 5:9). So when your life feels like a sealed scroll, remember that John's tears were answered, and yours matter to Him too. Keep your apron on, because this story is NOT over.
